intro: Your colleague Tom is out, and Sari calls with a message for him. Or the office WhatsApp group posts a long announcement in Indonesian, and Emma asks: what does it say? In this lesson you pass on whole messages and give the key facts of a notice in short, clear English. Warm-up: Sari says 'Saya sakit' — how do you tell Tom?
teachingNotes: Passing on a message has three parts: who + what they did, in the past simple because the call is finished (Sari called. Budi texted. Pak Hasan came at two.); the message itself in 1–3 short sentences (She can't come today. She's sick.); and what they want (Please call her back. Her number is …). The A1 lesson taught 'X says + fact' in the present; that is still fine, this lesson goes further to whole short messages.

Change the words for people: saya/aku → he or she; saya/-ku as owner (mobil saya) → his or her; me → him or her (Tolong telepon saya → Please call her back); kami → they. But kamu/Anda in a message FOR the listener stays you (Pak Hasan: 'Saya tunggu Bapak di lobi' → He's waiting for you in the lobby). Indonesian dia and -nya don't show man or woman, so check who sent the message: Sari → she/her, Budi → he/his. Common errors: *'Sari called. I can't come.', *'Sari … his car', *'Please call me back' (passed on unchanged), *'She sick' (no is), *'Sari call' (no -ed), *'She can't comes'.

Past simple from the chain: called, phoned, texted ('TEK-stid'), missed, came, went, had, got. Message content is often present (she's sick, he's in the lobby, she can't come). Limits: no reported-speech tense changes (said she was), no will, no going to, no present perfect. Plans are said with can or the present (He can come at three. The meeting is on Friday.). If a learner writes 'She said she is sick' / 'she was sick' or uses will correctly, accept it but don't teach the rule.

Summarising a notice: pick the 2–3 facts that matter, what, when, where (and what to do), and say them simply, not word for word. Skip the formal openings and closings of Indonesian notices: Dengan hormat, Diberitahukan kepada seluruh …, Demikian pengumuman ini, Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih, Mohon maaf atas ketidaknyamanannya. Word-for-word traps: air mati → There's no water / The water is off (never 'the water is dead'); listrik mati / mati lampu → There's no electricity / The power is off; sekolah libur → There's no school (not *'school is holiday'); diundur (to a later day) → The meeting is now on Wednesday; dibatalkan → cancelled (British) / canceled (American), or simply 'There's no …'.

Numbers and times as in a1-mediation-basic: 24-hour clock (14.00 → two p.m.), setengah (one hour less), rupiah. A time range 09.00–12.00 → from nine to twelve (from 9 a.m. to 12 noon); avoid '12 p.m.', which many people find confusing. British lift / American elevator. Encourage short sentences: one fact per sentence is clear and correct.

Feedback: any short natural sentence with the right facts is correct. Give partial credit when one key fact is missing (the time, the day) or a pronoun is wrong (I/my not changed, he for a woman); a word-for-word translation that is unclear ('the water is dead') loses most of the credit.

keyPoints.title: Who called, the message, what they want
keyPoints.explanation: Say who called (or texted, or came) in the past simple, because the call is finished: Sari called. Then give the message in short sentences, changing the words for people: I → he/she, my → his/her, me → him/her. But 'you' for the listener stays you. Then say what they want: Please call her back.

examples.en: Sari called. She can't come today. She's sick.
examples.id: Sari menelepon: 'Saya tidak bisa datang hari ini. Saya sakit.'

examples.en: Budi texted. He missed the bus. He's late.
examples.id: Budi kirim pesan: 'Saya ketinggalan bus. Saya terlambat.'

examples.en: Bu Ani called. Please call her back.
examples.id: Bu Ani menelepon: 'Tolong telepon saya kembali.'

id.title: Siapa yang menelepon, pesannya, apa maunya
id.explanation: Sebutkan siapa yang menelepon (atau kirim pesan, atau datang) dengan past simple, karena teleponnya sudah selesai: Sari called. Lalu sampaikan pesannya dalam kalimat pendek, dan ubah kata untuk orangnya: I → he/she, my → his/her, me → him/her. Tapi 'you' untuk orang yang kamu ajak bicara tetap you. Lalu sebutkan apa yang dia minta: Please call her back.

keyPoints.title: Only the key facts: what, when, where
keyPoints.explanation: Don't translate a notice word for word. Find what is happening, when and where (and what people must do), and say it in one or two short sentences. Skip the polite openings and closings (Dengan hormat, Diberitahukan kepada…, Atas perhatiannya…). Watch the word-for-word traps: air mati = There's no water; libur = There's no school; diundur ke Rabu = It's now on Wednesday.

examples.en: The office is closed on the first of May.
examples.id: Diberitahukan bahwa kantor tutup pada tanggal 1 Mei. Terima kasih.

examples.en: There's no yoga class on Saturday.
examples.id: Mohon maaf, kelas yoga hari Sabtu dibatalkan.

examples.en: The train to Bandung is thirty minutes late.

id.title: Hanya info penting: apa, kapan, di mana
id.explanation: Jangan terjemahkan pengumuman kata per kata. Cari apa yang terjadi, kapan dan di mana (dan apa yang harus dilakukan), lalu sampaikan dalam satu atau dua kalimat pendek. Lewati pembuka dan penutup yang sopan (Dengan hormat, Diberitahukan kepada…, Atas perhatiannya…). Hati-hati jebakan kata per kata: air mati = There's no water; libur = There's no school; diundur ke Rabu = It's now on Wednesday.

his mother is sick

assessment.prompt: Sari calls the office for Tom: 'Saya tidak bisa datang hari ini. Mobil saya rusak.' Complete the message for Tom: Sari called. She can't come today. ___ car is broken.
acceptableAnswers: her
her car is broken
assessment.rubric: Correct: her (Sari is a woman; 'saya' as owner becomes her). 'his' = 0 (Sari is not a man). 'my' = 0 (the message wasn't passed on). 'she' = 30 (right person, but the owner word is her).

blocks.text:
In the A1 lesson you said *Budi says he is late.* Now you pass on a **whole message**, for example when the phone rings and your colleague Tom is out. A good message has three parts:
- **Who + what they did**: *Sari called.* *Budi texted.* *Pak Hasan came at two.* Use the **past simple** (called, came), because the call or visit is **finished**.
- **The message**, in 1–3 short sentences: *She can't come today. She's sick.*
- **What they want**, if anything: *Please call her back. Her number is …*

id.text:
Di pelajaran A1 kamu bilang *Budi says he is late.* Sekarang kamu meneruskan **pesan utuh**, misalnya saat telepon berdering dan rekan kerjamu Tom sedang keluar. Pesan yang baik punya tiga bagian:
- **Siapa + apa yang dia lakukan**: *Sari called.* *Budi texted.* *Pak Hasan came at two.* Pakai **past simple** (called, came), karena telepon atau kunjungannya **sudah selesai**.
- **Isi pesannya**, dalam 1–3 kalimat pendek: *She can't come today. She's sick.*
- **Apa yang dia minta**, kalau ada: *Please call her back. Her number is …*

rows.en: Sari called. She can't come today. She's sick.
rows.id: Sari menelepon: 'Saya tidak bisa datang hari ini. Saya sakit.'

rows.en: Budi texted. He missed the bus. He's late.
rows.id: Budi kirim pesan: 'Saya ketinggalan bus. Saya terlambat.'
rows.note: texted = sent a text message; miss + ed

rows.en: Pak Hasan came at two. He had a question about the report.
rows.id: Pak Hasan datang jam 2. Dia mau tanya soal laporan.
rows.note: come → came, have → had (past forms to remember)

id.note: come → came, have → had (bentuk lampau yang dihafal)

rows.en: Bu Ani called. Please call her back. Her number is oh-eight-one-two, three-three-four-five, six-seven-eight-nine.
rows.id: Bu Ani menelepon: 'Tolong telepon saya kembali. Nomor saya 0812 3345 6789.'

blocks.text: **called, not call.** Indonesian says *Sari telepon tadi* with the same verb as today; only *tadi* shows the past. English changes the verb: *Sari **called**.* (call + ed, said 'kold'). *texted* is said 'TEK-stid' (one extra beat after t). And keep the message short: one fact per sentence is clear and easy to get right.

id.text: **called, bukan call.** Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Sari telepon tadi* dengan kata kerja yang sama seperti hari ini; hanya *tadi* yang menunjukkan lampau. Bahasa Inggris mengubah kata kerjanya: *Sari **called**.* (call + ed, dibaca 'kold'). *texted* dibaca 'TEK-stid' (ada satu ketukan tambahan setelah t). Dan buat pesannya pendek: satu info per kalimat itu jelas dan gampang benar.

blocks.prompt: Pak Dedi called the office an hour ago. How do you start the message for Tom?
blocks.explain: The call is finished, so use the past simple: call + ed = **called**. *Pak Dedi calls* means he calls often or always.

id.prompt: Pak Dedi menelepon kantor satu jam yang lalu. Bagaimana kamu memulai pesannya untuk Tom?
id.explain: Teleponnya sudah selesai, jadi pakai past simple: call + ed = **called**. *Pak Dedi calls* artinya dia sering atau selalu menelepon.

blocks.text:
The message is in the words of the **person who sent it**. When you pass it on, you're talking **about** that person, so the words for people change:
- **I → he / she**: *Saya sakit* → *She's sick.*
- **my → his / her** (the owner): *Mobil saya* → *his car / her car*
- **me → him / her** (after a verb like call): *Telepon saya* → *call her*
- **we → they**: *Kami terlambat* → *They're late.*
But **you** stays **you** when the message is for the person you're talking to: Pak Hasan to Tom, *'Saya tunggu Bapak di lobi'* → *He's waiting for you in the lobby.*

id.text:
Pesan itu ditulis dengan kata-kata **orang yang mengirimnya**. Saat kamu meneruskannya, kamu bicara **tentang** orang itu, jadi kata untuk orangnya berubah:
- **I → he / she**: *Saya sakit* → *She's sick.*
- **my → his / her** (pemilik): *Mobil saya* → *his car / her car*
- **me → him / her** (setelah kata kerja seperti call): *Telepon saya* → *call her*
- **we → they**: *Kami terlambat* → *They're late.*
Tapi **you** tetap **you** kalau pesannya untuk orang yang kamu ajak bicara: Pak Hasan ke Tom, *'Saya tunggu Bapak di lobi'* → *He's waiting for you in the lobby.*

rows.note: my → his; a phone with no battery is 'dead'

id.note: my → his; HP yang baterainya habis = 'dead'

rows.en: He's waiting for you in the lobby.
rows.id: Pak Hasan ke Tom: 'Saya tunggu Bapak di lobi.'
rows.note: the message is for Tom, so 'you' stays you

id.note: pesannya untuk Tom, jadi 'you' tetap you

blocks.text: **The dia / -nya trap.** Indonesian *dia* and *-nya* are the same for a man and a woman, so learners often say *his* for everyone. English must choose: look at **who sent the message**. Sari, Rina, Bu Ani → **she / her**. Budi, Dimas, Pak Hasan → **he / his / him**. And don't forget **is / are**: *Saya sakit* → *She **is** sick* (Indonesian has no 'to be').

id.text: **Jebakan dia / -nya.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia *dia* dan *-nya* sama untuk laki-laki dan perempuan, jadi banyak pelajar memakai *his* untuk semua orang. Bahasa Inggris harus memilih: lihat **siapa yang mengirim pesan**. Sari, Rina, Bu Ani → **she / her**. Budi, Dimas, Pak Hasan → **he / his / him**. Dan jangan lupa **is / are**: *Saya sakit* → *She **is** sick* (bahasa Indonesia tidak punya 'to be').

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani texts: 'Tas saya ketinggalan di ruang rapat.' Which sentence passes it on?
options: My bag is in the meeting room.
Her bag is in the meeting room.
His bag is in the meeting room.
blocks.explain: The message is from Bu Ani, a woman, so *saya* (the owner) becomes **her**. *My* would mean it's your bag; *his* is for a man.

id.prompt: Bu Ani kirim pesan: 'Tas saya ketinggalan di ruang rapat.' Kalimat mana yang meneruskannya dengan benar?
id.explain: Pesannya dari Bu Ani, seorang perempuan, jadi *saya* (pemilik) berubah jadi **her**. *My* berarti tasnya milikmu; *his* untuk laki-laki.

id.title: I berubah jadi he atau she

material.title: A notice: only the key facts

blocks.text:
Indonesian notices and group messages are often long and polite: *Dengan hormat, diberitahukan kepada seluruh karyawan bahwa …* and at the end *Demikian pengumuman ini. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.* Your English listener doesn't need all that. Ask three questions:
- **What?** (what happens or changes)
- **When?** (day, date, time)
- **Where?** (if it matters)
And sometimes **What do I do?** (*Please use the stairs.*). Then say the answers in **one or two short sentences**. This is a **summary** (ringkasan): the key facts, not every word.

id.text:
Pengumuman dan pesan grup dalam bahasa Indonesia sering panjang dan sopan: *Dengan hormat, diberitahukan kepada seluruh karyawan bahwa …* dan di akhir *Demikian pengumuman ini. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.* Pendengar bahasa Inggrismu tidak perlu semua itu. Tanyakan tiga hal:
- **What?** (apa yang terjadi atau berubah)
- **When?** (hari, tanggal, jam)
- **Where?** (kalau penting)
Dan kadang **What do I do?** (*Please use the stairs.*). Lalu sampaikan jawabannya dalam **satu atau dua kalimat pendek**. Ini namanya **summary** (ringkasan): info pentingnya saja, bukan setiap kata.

rows.en: The office is closed on the first of May.
rows.id: Diberitahukan kepada seluruh karyawan bahwa kantor tutup pada tanggal 1 Mei (Hari Buruh). Terima kasih.

rows.en: The train to Bandung is thirty minutes late.
rows.id: Mohon maaf, kereta tujuan Bandung mengalami keterlambatan 30 menit.

rows.en: The English class today is in room 2A at four p.m.
rows.id: Selamat siang. Info: kelas bahasa Inggris hari ini pindah ke ruang 2A, jam tetap 16.00. Terima kasih 🙏

blocks.prompt: The office group says: 'Dengan hormat, diberitahukan bahwa kantin tutup hari Senin karena renovasi. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.' Which is the best summary for Tom?
options: With respect, it is told that the canteen is closed. Thank you for your attention.
The canteen is closed on Monday.
The canteen is open on Monday.
blocks.explain: The key facts are what (the canteen is closed) and when (Monday). The first option translates the polite words one by one and loses the day; the last one says the opposite.

id.prompt: Grup kantor menulis: 'Dengan hormat, diberitahukan bahwa kantin tutup hari Senin karena renovasi. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.' Mana ringkasan terbaik untuk Tom?
id.explain: Info pentingnya: apa (kantin tutup) dan kapan (hari Senin). Pilihan pertama menerjemahkan kata-kata sopan satu per satu dan malah kehilangan harinya; pilihan terakhir artinya kebalikannya.

material.title: Notice words that don't translate word for word

blocks.text: Some words in Indonesian notices go wrong when you translate them word by word. **Air mati** is not *the water is dead*: say **There's no water** or **The water is off**. Learn these as phrases:

id.text: Beberapa kata di pengumuman bahasa Indonesia jadi salah kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata. **Air mati** bukan *the water is dead*: bilang **There's no water** atau **The water is off**. Hafalkan ini sebagai ungkapan:

rows.en: There's no water. / The water is off.
There's no electricity. / The power is off.
There's no school. / The school is closed.
The meeting is now on Wednesday.
The class is cancelled. / There's no class.
The lift is broken. Please use the stairs.
rows.id: lift sedang diperbaiki, silakan gunakan tangga

rows.note: 12.00 = twelve / midday; '12 p.m.' confuses many people

id.note: 12.00 = twelve / midday; '12 p.m.' membingungkan banyak orang

blocks.text: Notices often talk about **tomorrow** or **next week**, but you don't need a future form. Say it with the present and a time word, like a timetable: *The office **is** closed **tomorrow**. The meeting **is** on Friday.* Indonesian does the same: *Kantor tutup besok.*

id.text: Pengumuman sering membahas **besok** atau **minggu depan**, tapi kamu tidak perlu bentuk masa depan. Pakai present dan kata waktu, seperti jadwal: *The office **is** closed **tomorrow**. The meeting **is** on Friday.* Bahasa Indonesia juga begitu: *Kantor tutup besok.*

blocks.prompt: Your kos group says: 'Besok mati lampu jam 13.00–15.00.' What do you tell Tom?
options: Tomorrow the lamp is dead from one to three.
There's no electricity tomorrow from three to five.
There's no electricity tomorrow from one to three p.m.
blocks.explain: *Mati lampu* means there's no electricity, not a dead lamp. 13.00–15.00 = one to three p.m. (take away 12). The middle option has the wrong time.

id.prompt: Grup kos kamu menulis: 'Besok mati lampu jam 13.00–15.00.' Apa yang kamu sampaikan ke Tom?
id.explain: *Mati lampu* artinya listriknya padam, bukan lampunya mati. 13.00–15.00 = one to three p.m. (kurangi 12). Pilihan tengah jamnya salah.

id.title: Kata di pengumuman yang tidak bisa diterjemahkan kata per kata

suggestedQuestions: Can I say 'Sari says she is sick' instead of 'Sari called'?
How do I know if I should say he or she?
What can I skip in a long Indonesian announcement?
Why is 'the water is dead' wrong?

flashcards.back: There's no water. / The water is off.
The meeting is now on Wednesday.

resources.title: Leaving a message (A2 listening)
resources.note: A caller leaves a message for a colleague who is at lunch: listen for who called, what he wants and his phone number. Some phrases (I'll tell her, Could you…) are above this lesson: just notice them.

id.note: Seorang penelepon meninggalkan pesan untuk rekan kerja yang sedang makan siang: dengarkan siapa yang menelepon, apa maunya dan nomor teleponnya. Beberapa ungkapan (I'll tell her, Could you…) di atas level pelajaran ini: cukup perhatikan saja.

resources.title: An airport notice (A2 reading)
resources.note: Read a real-style notice about hand luggage and find the key facts. It uses must and numbers like 10kg; practise picking out only what matters.

id.note: Baca pengumuman bergaya asli tentang bagasi kabin dan cari info pentingnya. Di situ ada must dan angka seperti 10kg; latih dirimu memilih hanya yang penting.

id.intro: Rekan kerjamu Tom sedang keluar, lalu Sari menelepon dengan pesan untuknya. Atau grup WhatsApp kantor mengirim pengumuman panjang dalam bahasa Indonesia, dan Emma bertanya: isinya apa? Di pelajaran ini kamu meneruskan pesan utuh dan menyampaikan info penting dari pengumuman dalam bahasa Inggris yang pendek dan jelas. Pemanasan: Sari bilang 'Saya sakit' — bagaimana kamu menyampaikannya ke Tom?
suggestedQuestions: Boleh bilang 'Sari says she is sick' daripada 'Sari called'?
Bagaimana aku tahu harus pakai he atau she?
Apa saja yang boleh dilewati di pengumuman bahasa Indonesia yang panjang?

assessment.pmsg-1: Sari menelepon kantor untuk Tom: 'Saya tidak bisa datang hari ini. Mobil saya rusak.' Lengkapi pesan untuk Tom: Sari called. She can't come today. ___ car is broken.
assessment.pmsg-2: Pak Hasan menelepon saat Emma sedang keluar. Dia bilang: 'Tolong minta Bu Emma telepon saya kembali.' Tulis apa yang dia minta dalam satu kalimat bahasa Inggris setelah: Pak Hasan called.
assessment.pmsg-3: Budi kirim pesan ke kantor: 'Saya pergi ke Surabaya kemarin. Saya kembali ke kantor hari Senin.' Emma bertanya: Where's Budi? Tulis dua kalimat pendek dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.pmsg-4: Grup WhatsApp kantor: 'Pengumuman: rapat hari Selasa diundur ke hari Kamis jam 10. Terima kasih.' Emma bertanya: What's the message? Sampaikan info pentingnya dalam satu kalimat pendek bahasa Inggris.
assessment.pmsg-5: Pengumuman di gedung apartemenmu: 'PEMBERITAHUAN. Diberitahukan kepada seluruh penghuni bahwa air akan mati besok pukul 09.00–12.00 karena ada perbaikan pipa. Mohon maaf atas ketidaknyamanannya. — Pengelola Gedung.' Tetanggamu Tom bertanya: What does it say? Sampaikan info pentingnya dalam satu kalimat pendek bahasa Inggris.
assessment.pmsg-6: Anak laki-laki Emma sekolah di sekolah lokal. Sekolah mengirim pengumuman ini: 'Diberitahukan kepada Bapak/Ibu orang tua murid bahwa pada hari Jumat, 24 Oktober, sekolah libur karena ada rapat guru. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.' Sampaikan info pentingnya ke Emma dalam satu kalimat pendek bahasa Inggris.
